events.title: First Fleet Arrives at Sydney Cove
events.description: Captain Arthur Phillip led the British First Fleet ashore at Sydney Cove and raised the flag to begin the colony of New South Wales. The fleet carried convicts, marines and officials.
events.significance: The landing began British colonization of Australia. It had lasting and contested consequences for the Aboriginal peoples. The date is still marked in Australia each year.

events.title: Michigan Becomes the 26th U.S. State
events.description: Michigan was admitted to the Union as the 26th state. Its admission followed a long dispute with Ohio over the Toledo Strip.
events.significance: Michigan's admission extended the United States further into the Great Lakes region. The state later became a center of lumber, mining and automobile manufacturing.

events.title: The Cullinan Diamond Is Discovered
events.description: A surface inspection at the Premier Mine near Pretoria, South Africa, turned up an enormous rough diamond. At about 3,100 carats, it is the largest gem-quality diamond ever found.
events.significance: The stone was cut into several gems, including the Great Star of Africa. Those gems are now part of the British Crown Jewels.

events.title: India Becomes a Republic
events.description: India's constitution took effect, and the country formally became a sovereign republic. Rajendra Prasad was sworn in as its first president.
events.significance: The date is celebrated as Republic Day. It marks the point at which India's own constitution replaced the colonial-era framework of governance.
